In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in compensated chronic HF there is a preserved natriuretic response to volume expansion, which is modulated by the ANG II and the aldosterone concentrations, but that there is a blunted renal free water clearance in response to volume load.
the neuroendocrine and renal responses to intravascular volume load are altered in compensated HF.
volume expansion in compensated chronic heart disease patients is associated with a natriuresic response that may be modulated by the circulating ANG II and/or Aldo concentrations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
volume expansion in heart failure patients is natriuretic, which is in contrast with the findings in healthy controls.
in compensated HF the neuroendocrine response to volume expansion is intact, but renal function is impaired.
the volume sensor is intact in HF and that ANG II is an important modulator of renal sodium handling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neuroendocrine system in heart failure is intact and can respond normally to volume expansion.
the natriuresis in response to water immersion is blunted in patients with chronic heart failure (HF).
the neuroendocrine response to acute volume expansion in HF patients is similar to that of control subjects, and the natriuresis is attenuated by high ANG II and/or Aldo concentrations.
